Twin to Spirit; nearly 15-year Mars operation

Opportunity (MER-B) is a planetary rover built by NASA JPL in USA. Twin to Spirit; operated for nearly 15 years on Mars. Set the off-world driving record at 45.16 km and discovered hematite 'blueberries' indicating past water. Retired 2019.
Held the Mars driving record (45.16 km) until Perseverance passed it in October 2026; 14-year surface lifetime against a 90-sol design
Proposed NASA rover for the lunar south pole

Mars Exploration Rover B — the marathon rover. 5,111 sols of active operation (over 14 years), 45.16 km traversed (the most by any vehicle on another world until Perseverance passed it in October 2026). Confirmed past liquid water at Endurance, Victoria, and Endeavour craters. During the final 2018 dust storm, the rover's last telemetry showed depleted power — a moment poetically paraphrased as "my battery is low and it's getting dark."
